findings.what: verifyRecord accepts the legacy pre-verdict field set even when a verdict field is present, so a legacy-signed verdict record can still be edited from fail to pass and verify successfully.
findings.why: The loop over [SIGNED_FIELDS, LEGACY_SIGNED_FIELDS] lets the legacy MAC ignore verdict entirely. I reproduced a record signed over legacy fields with verdict:'fail', flipped it to verdict:'pass', and verifyRecord returned true; gauntlet-verify with requireSignature:true then reported status 'ran'. This weakens the sign-the-verdict mistake-class close for transition records.

findings.what: A bogus top_level_human_default is only rejected on the top_level_session branch; dispatch-channel derives still return ok:true for normal workers when the same trusted kernel value is bogus.
findings.why: validateRoleBindingValues only checks that top_level_human_default is a non-empty string, and the President-identity validation happens after the dispatched_worker branch. I reproduced deriveBinding({channel:'dispatch-claude', role:'backend-builder'}, {rb:{...RB, top_level_human_default:'made-up-super-role'}}) returning ok:true. That leaves a claimed trusted-kernel integrity failure outside the bridge fail-closed path.

parsed.summary: Round-1 alias, resolver-missing, corrupt-control, unknown-channel, authority-pollution, conformance extraction, and current-signature verdict-flip fixes are otherwise backed by focused tests/probes. The unified fix is still incomplete because legacy verdict signatures can be tampered and bogus top-level defaults are not global ED-220 failures for dispatch bridges.
